text:
anna_support: FYI — ACME support ticket: streaming responses randomly fail and show up as 5xx in our metrics. Customer says their client half-closes the connection and we report a 502/gateway error. They included request id `req_20260213_ACMEX-9f2b` and a short repro. Can SRE take a look?

mike_r: thanks — passing to oncall. do we have correlating traces? times?

anna_support: root ts is 2026-02-13T18:22:12Z, customer observes client abort at ~2s into stream. They used our streaming chat endpoint `POST /v1/chat/stream` w/ Transfer-Encoding: chunked. curl they used:

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream me"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

anna_support: customer says they close the socket intentionally after receiving first partial chunk and our metrics show 502s for those request ids.

julia_ml: quick thought — if client resets mid-stream and upstream runtime has already sent headers/body, the edge proxy might classify as 5xx if it sees a connection error. Could be NGINX/gateway mapping or our metric pipeline misclassifying client-aborts as server errors.

sre_oncall: I pulled logs for `req_20260213_ACMEX-9f2b`. runtime shows repeated: `send() failed: Broken pipe (errno 32)` during the stream. Gateway (edge-proxy) log shows: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` then we emit a 502 to client.

sre_oncall: snippet from runtime logs for the request:

```text
[2026-02-13T18:22:14Z] req=req_20260213_ACMEX-9f2b serving stream
[2026-02-13T18:22:15Z] req=req_20260213_ACMEX-9f2b send chunk size=1024
[2026-02-13T18:22:15Z] req=req_20260213_ACMEX-9f2b send() failed: Broken pipe (32)
[2026-02-13T18:22:15Z] req=req_20260213_ACMEX-9f2b connection reset by peer
```

sre_oncall: edge-proxy log line: `2026-02-13T18:22:15Z edge info: client closed connection while reading response; returning 502` — that message is unfortunate, it should be a 499-like classification but current code path converts this to 502 because the upstream closed unexpectedly.

mike_r: ok — two problems: 1) runtime sees EPIPE/broken pipe when client drops the socket (expected), 2) gateway interprets that as upstream error and surfaces 502. metrics pipeline counts 502 as server error. we should stop counting client-initiated disconnects as 5xx.

anna_support: customer is worried about billing — they're being charged and seeing failures in logs. we need to confirm if tokens were billed.

julia_ml: do we have request-to-charge mapping for partial streams? If runtime generated tokens before EPIPE, they may have been billed. need to check billing service hooks and whether we finalize charges on stream completion or on bytes produced.

sre_oncall: quick repro script to mimic their flow (client reads first chunk then closes):

```python
# simulate client that reads one chunk then closes
import socket, time
s = socket.socket()
s.connect(("api.redwood.ai", 443))
s.send(b"POST /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $KEY\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n")
# read first chunk
data = s.recv(4096)
print('got', len(data))
# close early
s.close()
```

sre_oncall: reproduced locally, same EPIPE on runtime and edge returned 502.

mike_r: next steps: 1) change edge behavior to treat downstream aborts differently — map to 499 and do not increment 5xx counters; 2) ensure billing behavior is clarified (bill for tokens produced, but don't surface as server error to customers); 3) add an instrumentation flag on runtime so it logs whether the disconnect was client-initiated vs upstream failure.

ops-bot: Note: edge service rollout `edge-v1.19.3` deployed 2026-02-11 03:05 UTC.

julia_ml: also check chunked transfer trailers or content-length assumptions — some clients send `Connection: close` semantics and the proxy mis-handles the half-close. If we can reproduce with plain curl + `--no-buffer` we should document supported client behavior.

anna_support: can we do a hotfix to stop these from counting in the 5xx alerting? customers are being paged.

sre_oncall: I can push a quick metrics filter: for any request with `connection reset by peer` within X seconds after first chunk, don't increment 5xx counter and mark as `client_aborted_stream`. I'll open a canary PR and schedule canary to 10% of traffic.

mike_r: thanks. also we should update alerting to exclude this new label for high-severity 5xx alerts.

julia_ml: longer-term: add a sentinel final chunk from runtime or use SSE/event-stream semantics where the server emits explicit `event: done` so clients can rely less on socket state. not blocking but worth exploring.

deploy-bot: Canaries scheduled: `edge-metrics-hotfix` -> 10% at 2026-02-14T09:00Z, rollback window 30m.

anna_support: I'd like to message ACME with: 1) explanation that client-aborts can look like server errors today, 2) mitigation timeline (metrics hotfix + doc), 3) whether they were billed. can someone own the customer comms?

mike_r: I'll own comms. will confirm billing with billing team after SRE confirms token finalize behavior.

sre_oncall: action items:
- SRE: open PR for metrics filter + canary (owner: @sre_oncall) — ETA 4h
- Runtime: add `client_abort` log field (owner: @julia_ml) — ETA 48h
- Billing: confirm how partial streams are charged (owner: @mike_r -> billing) — ETA 8h
- Support: draft customer note and send after SRE confirmation (owner: @mike_r) — ETA 24h

anna_support: thanks — please tag me on the PRs, I'll keep the customer updated.

mike_r: filing ticket in product: `SUP-4982` to improve streaming docs re: client disconnect semantics.

sre_oncall: deployed canary to 10% — initial telemetry looks good: 499-ish new label for client aborts, 5xx rate down for affected endpoints. I'll monitor for 60m and then ramp.

anna_support: awesome. once billing confirmed I'll close the ACME ticket. :thumbsup:

mike_r: closing loop — billing says tokens produced before the abort are billed (current behavior). billing will add a note to invoice if needed and we can offer refund case-by-case for this event.

anna_support: perfect. keep me posted on canary ramp and we'll update the customer after ramp completes.

sre_oncall: last note: we should also search for similar patterns in the last 30d (client-abort spike) and reevaluate alert thresholds. I'll add that to the follow-up.

anna_support: thanks team.
